title: VPC networking module — egress orchestration, endpoint failover & upgrade hooks
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provides opinionated VPC egress orchestration for Private deployments. The module will manage subnet roles, automated IGW/NAT replacement with zero-downtime failover, VPC endpoint provisioning and policies, dynamic route table attachment, and built-in healthchecks and upgrade hooks to support safe automated upgrades of networking components.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for AZ-aware subnet groups (public/private/isolation) and assigns route tables automatically
Supports configurable egress strategy: single IGW, multi-NAT per-AZ with failover, or NAT-less using Egress Gateway
Healthcheck integration: synthetic probe Lambda + CloudWatch metrics alarms per-AZ; automatically marks a NAT/route as degraded
Upgrade hook lifecycle: pre-upgrade verification, canary apply to single AZ, automated rollback on regression alarms
VPC endpoints can be created cross-account with policy templates and interface/ gateway endpoint toggles
Documentation and example for private deployment with Transit Gateway and cross-account endpoints
Module passes our internal terraform validate/lint and has CI plan/apply preview in a staging account
implementation_notes: Use terraform 1.5+ recommended features (for_each over resources, lifecycle blocks) and keep provider blocks minimal so consumers can override providers
Subnet role tagging convention: tag Role=redwood:subnet:{type} and allow consumers to supply suffixes
NAT replacement strategy: create replacement NAT in target AZ, warm up (create ENIs, run synthetic probe), switch route table association, then terminate old NAT
Healthchecks implemented as Lambda synthetic HTTP/TCP probes stored in a small module with CloudWatch alarms; alarms synthesized per resource with predictable naming
Upgrade hooks implemented as null_resource triggers that can be invoked by a separate orchestration pipeline (recommended pattern included in examples)
Provide careful defaults for IP addressing and avoid opinionated CIDR sharding — document recommended patterns instead of enforcing them
Ensure VPC endpoint policies are optional; provide prebuilt templates for S3/Dynamo/SecretsManager with least-privilege examples
decisions: Decision: prefer per-AZ NAT gateways over a single shared IGW NAT for HA by default to avoid cross-AZ egress bottlenecks
Decision: healthchecks run from inside the VPC using a lightweight Lambda per-AZ to detect local egress failures (preferred to external probes for egress path fidelity)
Decision: module will not manage Transit Gateway attachments; instead provide outputs consumable by TGW modules to avoid coupling
Decision: expose an opt-in 'canary_az' variable to run automatic canary upgrades rather than forcing canary behavior for every apply
risks: Changing route associations during NAT replacement can cause transient state where route tables are inconsistent — mitigated by warm-up and staged switch-over
Lambda-based healthchecks add IAM surface area; must follow least-privilege and use customer-managed KMS where required
Automating cross-account endpoint creation requires careful org permissions and may fail if consumer account lacks required IAM roles
Terraform state drift if consumers manually modify low-level resources — mitigate with clear docs and strong examples
